checked_claims: AFI credits Natalie Wood as Maria and confirms Marni Nixon dubbed Wood's singing voice.
AFI and the Academy page support the stage-musical basis, Jets-Sharks conflict, author credits, and the 1961 film's role distinctions.
AFI supports Rachel Zegler as Maria in the 2021 film, so the body accurately explains why the year matters.
items.distractor_review: Rita Moreno played Anita, Richard Beymer played Tony, and Marni Nixon supplied Wood's singing voice. Natalie Wood is the only screen performer of Maria in the stated 1961 film.

checked_claims: AFI credits James Dean as Jim Stark, Natalie Wood as Judy, Sal Mineo as Plato, and Nicholas Ray as director.
AFI supports the twenty-four-hour story span and the three-frame police-station staging.
AFI and the Academy collection support Griffith Observatory and the cited collection objects; the body makes no Oscar-nomination claim for Dean.
items.distractor_review: Sal Mineo played Plato, Natalie Wood played Judy, and Dennis Hopper was a Goon. James Dean uniquely played Jim Stark.

source_limits.reason: The page's statement that the latter two of Dean's three films earned Oscar nominations is historically incorrect. The article does not repeat it and uses only the separately displayed collection/location material.

checked_claims: AFI credits Anthony Perkins as Norman Bates, Hitchcock as director, and Joseph Stefano as writer; it identifies Bloch's 1959 novel as the source.
AFI supports the character adaptation, Perkins casting connection, and Saul Bass's opening-title design.
The Academy Hitchcock collection supports Psycho's place in the 1958–1963 period, censorship context, and innovative promotion.
items.distractor_review: Vera Miles played Lila Crane, John Gavin played Sam Loomis, and Martin Balsam played Milton Arbogast. Anthony Perkins is the unique Norman Bates answer.

checked_claims: AFI credits Humphrey Bogart as Samuel Spade, Peter Lorre as Joel Cairo, and Sydney Greenstreet as Kasper Gutman.
AFI supports the 1930 Hammett novel, earlier Warner adaptations in 1931 and 1936, Huston's directorial debut, Greenstreet's film debut, and the nomination claims.
The displayed Academy digital-collection URL redirected to a generic welcome page and did not expose the claimed press release or nomination evidence.
items.distractor_review: Mary Astor played Brigid O'Shaughnessy, Peter Lorre played Joel Cairo, and Sydney Greenstreet played Kasper Gutman. Humphrey Bogart alone played Sam Spade.
